Therefrom
thare-from'
adv. (from that; the word of the charge not to turn aside from the law, and of the kings who did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam)
A compound of there and from, on the pattern of thereof, therein, thereat, thereto — a demonstrative adverb meaning from that. The Hebrew idiom is sur min, to turn aside from, or lo sar min, he departed not from.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The same word marks the best and the worst of Israel's history, and the contrast is deliberate. Joshua's farewell charge: “Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left” (Joshua 23:6), repeating Moses in Deuteronomy 5:32. Two things are worth noting: courage is required to keep a law, not merely to fight a battle; and the departure may be in either direction, adding to the law being as much a turning aside as subtracting. Then the identical construction becomes the historian's standing verdict on the kings of Israel. Of Jehoram: “Nevertheless he cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom” (2 Kings 3:3). Of Jehoahaz: “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom” (2 Kings 13:2). The formula recurs through the northern kingdom until the exile: a whole dynasty of men who did not depart from a sin instituted two centuries earlier for reasons of state.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines therefrom as from this or from that, and lists it among the demonstrative compounds thereof, therein, thereat, and thereto.

THEREFROM, adv. From this or from that.

Turn not aside therefrom, to the right hand or to the left. Josh. 23.

THEREOF, adv. Of that or this.

THEREIN, adv. In that or this place, time or thing.

THERETO, adv. To that or this.

Key Scripture

Joshua 23:6 — "Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left;"

Deuteronomy 5:32 — "Ye shall observe to do therefore as the LORD your God hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left."

2 Kings 3:3 — "Nevertheless he cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom."

2 Kings 13:2 — "And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, which made Israel to sin; he departed not therefrom."

Modern Corruption

Departures from Scripture are imagined as running in one direction only, so a church guards one flank and loses the other.

expand to see more

To the right hand or to the left is a formula, and it is exact. Turning aside from God's word is possible in two directions, and every generation of the church watches one of them intently while walking off the other. The party alarmed by liberalism polices subtraction — the doctrines quietly dropped — and adds requirements Scripture never made, binding consciences on matters God left free. The party alarmed by legalism polices addition and quietly lets the hard commands go. Joshua's charge covers both by naming the road rather than the ditch: keep and do all that is written, and turn aside neither way.

The Jeroboam formula shows how a departure becomes permanent. Jeroboam set up calves at Bethel and Dan for a stated political reason — lest the people go up to Jerusalem to sacrifice and their hearts turn again to the house of David — and every northern king after him inherited the arrangement and kept it. The historian's refrain is not that they invented new wickedness but that they departed not therefrom. Institutional sin is rarely re-decided; it is simply not departed from, and the men who maintain it usually have no strong feelings about it at all. It required courage to keep the law, exactly as Joshua said, and no courage whatever to leave the calves standing.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew sur min, to turn aside from — Joshua 23:6; lo sar min, he departed not from — 2 Kings 3:3, 13:2; dabaq, to cleave — 2 Kings 3:3.

expand to see more

Hebrew sur — to turn aside, depart; the verb in both the charge and the verdict.

Hebrew yamin u-semol — right hand and left; the two directions of departure.

Hebrew dabaq — to cling, cleave; 2 Kings 3:3, of Jehoram cleaving to Jeroboam's sins.

Hebrew chazaq — to be strong, courageous; Joshua 23:6, required for keeping the law.

English there- compounds — thereof, therein, thereat, therefrom — ordinary in 1611.

Usage

"“Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written” — courage, for a law."

"“To the right hand or to the left” — departure runs in two directions."

"“He departed not therefrom” — the refrain over a whole dynasty."
